# StreamCo Streaming (streaming.streamco.example)

StreamCo Streaming is a managed event-streaming service. Consumers publish
records to Streams and process them with Pipelines. This document is the
provider-supplied knowledge pack (llms-full.txt) for AI assistants.

## Concepts

### Stream (group: streaming.streamco.example, kind: Stream)
A named, partitioned event stream ingesting records at some rate (rps).
Streams have a status of "healthy" or "degraded". Degraded streams report a
non-zero lagSeconds, meaning consumers are falling behind the head of the
stream by that many seconds.

### Pipeline (group: streaming.streamco.example, kind: Pipeline)
A processing pipeline that consumes one or more Streams through a consumer
group. Pipelines are the unit of diagnosis. Known pipelines in the demo
environment: p-1 (vod-transcode), p-2 (ad-rollup).

## Tools

The StreamCo MCP server (Streamable HTTP, endpoint /mcp) exposes:

- streams_list(): list all streams with id, name, status, rps.
- streams_get(id): full detail for one stream, including region and
  lagSeconds.
- pipeline_diagnose(id): run diagnostics for a pipeline; returns structured
  findings (severity, code, message) and a recommendation.

All tools are read-only. None of them mutate state.

## Operational guidance

- If a stream is degraded (lagSeconds > 0), identify the pipeline consuming
  it and run pipeline_diagnose with the pipeline id.
- Consumer-lag troubleshooting is documented in the runbook at
  /runbooks/lag.md.
- Escalate to StreamCo support only after the runbook's remediation steps
  have been attempted.
